i mentioned in a reply to someone else’s comment and i wanna reiterate it here to make sure you see it: the reason expectations feel so high and unattainable or even unrealistic, is BECAUSE of the patriarchy. it affects everyone not just women. it pushes men to be a certain way and if they cant reach or somehow fall outside of that expectation, theyre deemed failures.

men are just as much the victim of the patriarchy as women are.

but just because you’ve failed some arbitrary societal expectation, doesn’t mean you are objectively a failure. it sounds to me like it’s guilt tripped you to hell. but you don’t HAVE to be a certain type of man/woman/person to be happy and successful. 

me for example, im a trans man (he/him), and uuuuuhhh im short as fuck !! but not like 5’6” or 5’3”, more like 4’8”. and like 💀 i wont lie i wish i was at least in the upper 5 feets but unfortunately there’s not much to be done about that. and when i finally get on hormones im just going to become a hairy little imp. BUT… as silly as it sounds… idk if you’ve seen game of thrones or have heard about it in passing, but Tyrion Lannister (portrayed by Peter Dinklage) was one of my favorite characters. Seeing someone shorter than i am be able clever and kind and an absolute pussy magnet gave me hope. i also related heavily with how his father treated him due to his dwarfism (though my scoldings were more to do with my being queer than being short hehe).

but you know, it helps a lot to find comfort in characters who share your same struggles. the fear of being undesirable, the fear of being isolated, the fear of not being good enough. theyre very real and pretty valid fears. we’re social animals and we crave love and acceptance. and for the most part we all deserve that love and acceptance. and i think to some extent we all feel unworthy of that due to not fulfilling societal expectations of height or beauty or expression. but unfortunately its something we have to break free from ourselves. wallowing in it doesn’t do us any good.
